title: Elon Musk on How to Build the Future: Usefulness, Fearlessness, and the Factory
summary: Musk explains how to choose what to work on (maximize usefulness: utility delta times people affected), how to act despite fear by accepting low odds, why technology decays without hard work, and why he spends 80% of his time on engineering and sees the factory as harder than the product.

principles.text: Pick work by usefulness: the improvement over the state of the art times the number of people affected.
principles.quote: what would be the utility Delta compared to the current state-of-the-art times how many people it would affect

principles.text: Small benefit to many people can be worth as much as a big benefit to few; you don't need to change the world.
principles.quote: if it has a small amount of good for a large number of people that's I mean I think that's that's fine like stuff doesn't need to be change the world just to be good

principles.text: Do important things despite fear; accepting low odds (fatalism) reduces the fear.
principles.quote: there are times when something is important enough you believe in it enough that you do it in spite of the fear

principles.text: Optimizing for risk-adjusted return isn't always the goal; mission can justify low-probability ventures.
principles.quote: if the objective was to achieve the best risk adjusted return sliding our company is insane but that was not that was not my objective

principles.text: Technology doesn't improve on its own; it only gets better when smart people work relentlessly, and otherwise it decays.
principles.quote: it only gets better if smart people work work like crazy to make it better that's how any technology actually gets better

principles.text: A founder should spend most time on engineering and design, and the factory (the machine that builds the machine) is harder than the product.
principles.quote: what really matters is that is the machine that builds the machine the factory and this that is at least towards my to eat harder than the vehicle itself
